balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Sumitomo Chemical Co., Ltd.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Sumitomo Chemical Co., Ltd.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Sumitomo Chemical Co., Ltd.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Sumitomo Chemical Co., Ltd.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Sumitomo Chemical Co., Ltd.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Sumitomo Chemical Co., Ltd.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Sumitomo Chemical Co., Ltd.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Sumitomo Chemical Co., Ltd.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

segmentRevenueOld.title: Segment revenue (old structure, through FY2024)
segmentRevenueOld.content:
Sumitomo Chemical reported five business segments through FY2024: Essential Chemicals (basic petrochemicals), Energy & Functional Materials, IT-related Chemicals, Health & Crop Sciences, and Pharmaceuticals (majority-owned Sumitomo Pharma).

For Sumitomo Chemical Co., Ltd.: Essential Chemicals is the most cyclical segment, tracking naphtha/petrochemical spreads; Health & Crop Sciences and Pharmaceuticals are the defensive counterweight.

What to watch:

  • Essential Chemicals swinging between the segments' largest profit and largest loss across the cycle
  • Pharmaceuticals' share of group profit before the FY2025 reorganisation

segmentProfitOld.title: Segment operating profit (old structure, through FY2024)
segmentProfitOld.content:
Operating profit by the same five segments as the revenue chart above -- the split shows which businesses actually made money, not just which were largest by sales.

For Sumitomo Chemical Co., Ltd.: FY2024 shows both of the group's two largest segments turning loss-making in the same year -- Essential Chemicals on the petrochemical downturn and Pharmaceuticals on an impairment -- the immediate backdrop to the FY2025 reorganisation.

What to watch:

  • Segments with revenue share far exceeding profit share (margin-dilutive)
  • One-off impairments distorting a single year

segmentRevenueNew.title: Segment revenue (new structure, FY2025 onward)
segmentRevenueNew.content:
From FY2025 Sumitomo Chemical regrouped into five new segments: Essential Green Materials (petrochemicals, repositioned toward sustainability), ICT/Mobility Solutions, Agro-Life Solutions (the former Health & Crop Sciences), Advanced Medical Solutions, and Sumitomo Pharma (the former Pharmaceuticals segment, now reported standalone).

For Sumitomo Chemical Co., Ltd.: this structure is not comparable to the pre-FY2025 segments above -- names and the businesses rolled into them both changed, so no YoY growth is computed across the FY2024/FY2025 boundary.

What to watch:

  • Agro-Life Solutions as the largest and steadiest segment
  • Sumitomo Pharma's recovery now that it is split out from the old Pharmaceuticals segment's writedown

segmentProfitNew.title: Segment operating profit (new structure, FY2025 onward)
segmentProfitNew.content:
Operating profit by the new five-segment structure introduced in FY2025 -- only two years of data exist so far, too short to judge a trend, but useful to see which segments are carrying the group.

For Sumitomo Chemical Co., Ltd.: Essential Green Materials posted a large FY2025 loss while Sumitomo Pharma and ICT/Mobility Solutions carried the group's profit -- the opposite mix to the old structure's Essential Chemicals-led profit.

What to watch:

  • Whether Essential Green Materials returns to profit as the petrochemical cycle turns
  • Sumitomo Pharma's profit trend now reported on its own line

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Sumitomo Chemical Co., Ltd.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Sumitomo Chemical Co., Ltd.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
